title: The store on a schedule for this Mac
request: After the store check: make sure the store runs on a schedule.
plan: Reuse the conductor's own due rule
A launchd job every 6 hours, low priority
Never two runs at once; stop under 2 GB free

decisions.why: a whole run took 91 minutes under load; the worker already runs hourly while the server runs

decisions.decision: Skip while the server's worker runs
decisions.why: the worker runs the store inside its own process, which a check for another store run would not see; two runs would do the same work twice

findings.defect: a check for another store run would miss the worker's run
findings.scenario: the server's worker runs conduct inside python -m dclab_rnd.worker; pgrep for the store's command finds nothing
findings.cause: the worker is its own process
findings.fix: the schedule skips while the worker runs

measurements.name: the first whole run after 32.33 to 32.36
measurements.gate: the run ends without a failed step and builds the DCLab Code sets
measurements.result: 91 minutes, no failed step; dclab_code kept 4 sources; sets: m6 2 episodes, m7 8 judged steps, m2 8 and m1 8 permission decisions; the tutor waits for 20 rows

outcome: The store runs every 6 hours on the owner's Mac without the server, alone and with disk to spare.
lessons: A schedule must know every way the same job is already started
risks: a run started while the Mac sleeps waits for the next interval
